Bug_Details: Duration.from(Duration) returns itself; from(Period) throws a runtime exception. Duration.from(TemporalAmount) will always throw a UnsupportedTemporalTypeException when passed a Period and return itself when passed a Duration.
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates the incorrect behavior of Duration.from when dealing with TemporalAmount subclasses. Duration.from(Duration) returns the input Duration itself, which is correct. However, Duration.from(Period) throws an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException, demonstrating the bug when trying to convert a Period to a Duration.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug2 method triggers the bug by passing a Period to the showBug2 method, which in turn calls Duration.from(period). This call results in an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException because Duration.from cannot handle Period objects.
